base-devel: A bundle of the basic tools needed to build programs from source.
git: Tracks changes in code and downloads projects from sites like GitHub.
gcc: The compiler that turns C and C++ code into a runnable program.
gcc-libs: Runtime pieces of the GCC compiler that many programs need to run.
clang: An alternative compiler for C and C++, used to build programs.
make: Runs the build steps of a project in the right order.
cmake: A tool that prepares a project to be built; needed only to build.
meson: A build system used by many modern programs; needed only to build.
ninja: A fast helper that runs the build steps; needed only to build.
pkgconf: Helps the build find the libraries that are installed.
autoconf: Generates configuration scripts for building older-style projects.
automake: Generates build files for older-style projects.
patch: Applies small corrections (patches) to source code files.
binutils: Low-level tools used to build and inspect programs.
linux-headers: Files needed to build drivers and modules for the running kernel.
dkms: Rebuilds extra kernel drivers automatically when the kernel updates. It runs with full system access.
python: The Python language; many tools and scripts need it to run.
python-pip: Downloads and installs extra Python libraries.
python-setuptools: Helps package and install Python programs; usually needed to build.
python-wheel: Builds Python packages; needed only to build.
python-build: Builds Python packages; needed only to build.
python-installer: Installs built Python packages; needed only to build.
python-gobject: Lets Python programs use the GNOME/GTK graphics libraries.
python-requests: Lets Python programs talk to websites and web services.
python-pyqt5: Lets Python programs build windows with the Qt 5 toolkit.
python-pyqt6: Lets Python programs build windows with the Qt 6 toolkit.
python-numpy: Fast math on large lists of numbers, used by scientific tools.
nodejs: Runs JavaScript programs outside the browser.
npm: Downloads JavaScript libraries; often runs during a build.
rust: The Rust language and compiler; needed to build Rust programs.
cargo: Rust's build and download tool; fetches libraries while building.
go: The Go language and compiler; needed to build Go programs.
jdk-openjdk: The Java development kit, used to build and run Java programs.
perl: The Perl language, used by many older scripts and tools.
lua: A small scripting language built into many programs.
bash: The command-line shell most scripts run in.
glibc: The core system library almost every program uses.
coreutils: Basic commands like ls, cp and mv.
sudo: Lets you run a command as the administrator.
polkit: Asks for your password when a program needs admin rights.
systemd: The service manager that starts and supervises system services.
systemd-libs: Library pieces of systemd that other programs use.
dbus: The message bus programs use to talk to each other.
util-linux: A set of everyday system tools, like mount and lsblk.
openssh: Secure remote login and file copy over the network.
gnupg: Encrypts data and checks digital signatures.
openssl: The library that provides encryption for secure connections.
curl: Downloads files and talks to websites from the command line.
wget: Downloads files from the web from the command line.
fuse2: Lets programs such as AppImages mount their own files.
fuse3: Lets programs provide their own file systems.
docker: Runs programs in isolated containers; the service needs administrator rights.
zlib: Compresses and decompresses data; used by a huge number of programs.
sqlite: A small database engine that many programs embed.
xdg-utils: Lets programs open links and files with your default apps.
hicolor-icon-theme: The fallback icon set every program can use.
desktop-file-utils: Helps register programs in the application menu.
shared-mime-info: Tells the system which program opens which file type.
libappindicator-gtk3: Lets programs put an icon in the system tray.
qt5-base: The Qt 5 toolkit most KDE-style programs use for windows.
qt6-base: The Qt 6 toolkit most KDE-style programs use for windows.
qt6-declarative: The part of Qt 6 that draws modern QML interfaces.
qt6-svg: Lets Qt 6 programs show SVG images.
qt6-wayland: Lets Qt 6 programs run on the Wayland display system.
gtk3: The GTK 3 toolkit used by many GNOME-style programs for windows.
gtk4: The GTK 4 toolkit used by modern GNOME-style programs for windows.
glib2: A base library that many Linux programs are built on.
wayland: The modern system that draws windows on screen.
mesa: The open-source graphics drivers for 3D and video.
vulkan-icd-loader: Lets programs use the Vulkan graphics interface, common in games.
libx11: The base library for the older X11 display system.
libxcb: A low-level library for talking to the X11 display system.
xorg-server: The older display server that draws windows on screen.
cairo: A library for drawing 2D graphics and text.
pango: A library for laying out and drawing text.
fontconfig: Finds the fonts installed on the system.
freetype2: Draws the letters of fonts on screen.
harfbuzz: Shapes text so letters and accents are placed correctly.
gdk-pixbuf2: Loads images (PNG, JPEG...) for GTK programs.
libjpeg-turbo: Reads and writes JPEG images quickly.
imagemagick: Converts and edits images from the command line.
electron: A packaged web browser engine that many desktop apps are built on; big download.
nss: Security library with certificates and encryption that browsers use.
nspr: A support library used by browsers and security software.
ffmpeg: Converts and plays almost any audio and video format.
vlc: A media player that plays almost anything.
gstreamer: A framework that lets programs play and process audio and video.
pipewire: The system that routes sound and screen sharing between programs.
pipewire-pulse: Lets older sound programs work with PipeWire.
libpulse: Library that lets programs play sound through PulseAudio or PipeWire.
alsa-lib: The base library for sound on Linux.
wine: Runs many Windows programs on Linux.
steam: The Steam game store and launcher.
lib32-mesa: 32-bit graphics drivers that older games and Wine need.
yay: A helper that installs packages from the AUR.
paru: A helper that installs packages from the AUR.
flatpak: Installs sandboxed apps from Flathub and other sources.
noto-fonts: A large set of fonts covering most languages.
ttf-liberation: Fonts that look like Arial and Times New Roman.
libx264: Encodes video in the common H.264 format.
libsecret: Lets programs store passwords safely in your keyring.
libgit2: A library that lets programs work with git repositories.
suffix:-git: A development build taken straight from the project's latest code. It changes constantly and has not been tested as a release.
suffix:-bin: A ready-made program downloaded from the developer, not built on your machine. You trust the developer's file.
suffix:-docs: The manual and documentation for a program; not needed to run it.
suffix:-dev: Files for programmers who build software with this library.
suffix:-dkms: A driver that is rebuilt for your kernel automatically. It loads into the kernel with full system access.
prefix:lib32-: The 32-bit version of a library, needed by older games and Wine.
prefix:lib: A library: shared code that other programs use. It does nothing alone.
prefix:python-: A Python library or tool that other programs use.
prefix:perl-: A Perl library that other programs use.
prefix:ruby-: A Ruby library that other programs use.
prefix:noto-fonts: Fonts that cover many languages and symbols.
prefix:qt5-: A piece of the Qt 5 toolkit used to draw program windows.
prefix:qt6-: A piece of the Qt 6 toolkit used to draw program windows.
prefix:gtk: A piece of the GTK toolkit used to draw program windows.
prefix:gst-: A plug-in that teaches GStreamer more audio or video formats.
prefix:kf5: A building block from KDE Frameworks 5, shared by KDE programs.
prefix:kf6: A building block from KDE Frameworks 6, shared by KDE programs.
prefix:xorg-: A part of the older X11 display system.
prefix:xdg-desktop-portal: Lets sandboxed apps ask your desktop for things like file pickers and screen sharing.
prefix:linux-: A Linux kernel or something tied to one. Installing it changes how the system boots.
prefix:nvidia: A driver for NVIDIA graphics cards. It loads into the kernel with full system access.
